name: Support Ticket
description: Log customer support tickets with category, priority, affected product, steps to reproduce and screenshot attachments.
seoDescription: Support ticket form template that collects the issue category, priority, product, steps to reproduce and screenshots, so your team can triage tickets faster.
thumbnailAlt: Support Ticket form beside a photo of a support agent working at his desk

content.intro: A support ticket form is a form that collects a customer's contact details, the issue category, its priority and the steps that led to the problem so a support team can route and fix it without a long back-and-forth. This template asks for the account email, product area and impact up front, then lets customers attach screenshots or log files in the same submission.
content.audience: SaaS support teams, e-commerce customer service desks, agencies running client support and small product teams without a full help desk tool.
useCases: A 'Contact support' link in your app or help center footer
Bug reports from beta testers with screenshots attached
Billing and account questions routed to a separate queue by category
Client support for agencies that maintain websites or apps
tips: Use conditional logic to show the 'Steps to reproduce' question only when the category is 'Bug or error', so billing questions stay short.
Connect a webhook or the Google Sheets plugin to drop each ticket into your queue, and turn on the respondent email copy so customers keep a record of what they sent.
Edit responses to add an internal status and keep the full edit history of who changed what on each ticket.

faq.question: What should a support ticket form include?
faq.answer: The customer's name and email, the account or order ID, an issue category, a priority or impact level, the product area, a clear description, steps to reproduce, and an optional screenshot or file upload. These let an agent triage the ticket on first read.

faq.question: How should support ticket priority levels be defined?
faq.answer: Most teams use four levels: Urgent (the product is down or data is at risk), High (a key feature is broken with no workaround), Normal (a problem with a workaround) and Low (a question or request). Describe each level in the option text so customers pick consistently.

faq.question: Can customers attach screenshots to a ticket?
faq.answer: Yes. The template includes a file upload field for up to three images or PDFs, and uploads are stored privately so only your team can open them.

faq.question: Can I use this instead of a help desk tool?
faq.answer: For a small team, yes: tickets arrive by email notification, sit in a response table you can filter and export, and can be pushed to other tools by webhook. Larger teams often use the form as the intake step for an existing help desk.

fields.label: Account email
fields.hint: The email you sign in with

fields.label: Order or account ID
fields.hint: Optional. Helps us find your account faster

fields.label: How much is this affecting you?
options: Low - a question or small annoyance
Normal - something is wrong but I have a workaround
High - a key feature is broken, no workaround
Urgent - the product is down or data is at risk

fields.label: Subject
fields.placeholder: e.g. CSV export fails with error 500

fields.label: Describe the problem
fields.placeholder: What happened, and what did you expect to happen?

fields.label: Screenshots or files
fields.hint: Optional. Up to 3 files, 10 MB each
